content.title: About
content.content: Veal Cordon Bleu is a classic French dish consisting of a thinly pounded veal cutlet stuffed with ham and melted cheese, coated in breadcrumbs and fried until golden. It is served hot, often with a sauce and a side.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in the early 1920s in Switzerland before becoming popular in France.
Traditional cheeses used are Swiss Emmental or Gruyère.
A chicken version, "Chicken Cordon Bleu," is now common in mass‑market cuisine.
The veal should be pounded to about 0.5 cm thickness for tenderness.
In the United States it is frequently served with mushroom sauce or Béarnaise.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Veal and cheese provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Veal contains vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Melted cheese adds calcium, important for bone health.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Veal is a good source of heme iron, which is readily absorbed.

items.title: Zinc content
items.content: Zinc supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: The dish is prepared with butter and cheese, making it calorie‑dense; portion control is advised for weight‑watchers.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Risk of undercooked meat
items.content: Veal must be fully cooked to prevent food‑borne illnesses.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Ham and cheese are often salty, increasing the dish’s sodium content.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Veal Cordon Bleu hot, sliced into portions. It pairs well with mashed potatoes, vegetable ragout, fresh salad, or rice. Mushroom, creamy, mustard, or classic Béarnaise sauces enhance the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. For freezing, wrap tightly in plastic film and aluminum foil; keep up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before serving.
